key_insight: EdgeRefine improves the privacy-utility trade-off for graph learning by ranking and sampling edges with Jaccard-based probability estimates instead of adding uniform noise to the entire adjacency matrix.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical edge-differentially-private preprocessing strategy for GNN pipelines that can preserve model accuracy while limiting structural privacy leakage.
method: Estimate edge-existence probabilities using Jaccard similarity.
Rank edges for noisy removal and sample true vs. false edges separately using the privacy budget ε.
Control final graph sparsity with a separate sampling rate k.
evidence_signal: Across node and graph classification experiments, EdgeRefine matches or approaches non-private accuracy and outperforms privacy-preserving baselines; at ε=2.5 it improves accuracy by 17.8% on ACM with GAT and 19.7% on Cora with GCN, while also resisting reconstruction attacks.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of Jaccard-based edge ranking and the chosen ε/k settings, so graphs with weak local similarity signals may be harder to refine effectively.
paper_title: EdgeRefine: Privacy-Utility Balance for Graphs via Jaccard Sampling under Edge Differential Privacy
